pulserver.pypulseq.make_phase_blip

Contents

  • make_phase_blip()

pulserver.pypulseq.make_phase_blip#

pulserver.pypulseq.make_phase_blip(system, axis, fov, *, steps=1.0, duration=None)#

Create a phase blip spanning steps Cartesian k-space cells.

The short gradient played between echoes of a train to advance the phase encode. Stated in cells rather than area: one cell is 1 / fov, so a blip of steps=1 moves one line and steps=R implements an acceleration of R without any further arithmetic. Negative steps blip backwards.

Parameters:

  • system (pypulseq.Opts) – System limits.

  • axis (str) – Gradient channel ("x", "y", or "z").

  • fov (float) – Field of view along axis (m); one k-space cell is 1 / fov.

  • steps (float, optional) – Cells to traverse; non-zero, may be negative.

  • duration (float or None, optional) – Force a blip duration (s); None uses the shortest feasible.

Returns:

SimpleNamespace – Blip trapezoid with area steps / fov.

Examples

>>> import pypulseq as pp_up
>>> from pulserver.pypulseq import make_phase_blip
>>> blip = make_phase_blip(pp_up.Opts(), "y", 0.24, steps=2)
>>> round(blip.area, 3)
8.333

Blip by the increments a sampling plan prescribes:

for step in plan.increments(shot)[:, 0]:
    seq.add_block(make_phase_blip(system, "y", fov, steps=step))

(png)

See also

make_phase_encoding

the full-area encode used once per shot.
